cite: P. Ladisa, H. Plate, M. Martinez, and O. Barais, "SoK: Taxonomy of attacks on open-source software supply chains," in Proc. IEEE Symp. Security and Privacy (SP), 2023, pp. 1509–1526.
contrib: Attack-tree taxonomy: 107 attack vectors, 94 real incidents, 33 safeguards across the OSS supply chain.
gap: Catalogues safeguards but no single client-side system combines them; Loom composes five of them.

cite: P. Ladisa, S. E. Ponta, N. Ronzoni, M. Martinez, and O. Barais, "On the feasibility of cross-language detection of malicious packages in npm and PyPI," in Proc. 39th Annu. Computer Security Applications Conf. (ACSAC), 2023.
contrib: Language-independent ML features detect malicious npm/PyPI packages; found 58 previously unknown malicious packages.
gap: Detection is probabilistic and evadable; Loom contains and verifies instead of classifying.

cite: W. Guo, Z. Xu, C. Liu, C. Huang, Y. Fang, and Y. Liu, "An empirical study of malicious code in PyPI ecosystem," in Proc. 38th IEEE/ACM Int. Conf. Automated Software Engineering (ASE), 2023.
contrib: 4,669 malicious package files; >50% show multiple behaviours, with credential theft and command execution most common; 74.81% reached users via source installation.
gap: Source-install is the dominant infection path, which is exactly what AUR helpers do; motivates Heddle.

cite: X. Zhou, Y. Zhang, W. Niu, J. Liu, H. Wang, and Q. Li, "An analysis of malicious packages in open-source software in the wild," in Proc. 55th Annu. IEEE/IFIP Int. Conf. Dependable Systems and Networks (DSN), 2025.
contrib: Largest dataset: 24,356 malicious packages; knowledge-graph analysis shows heavy code reuse and dependency-hidden malware.
gap: Security reports are the only reliable context source; ecosystems lack preventive, verifiable controls.

cite: P. Przymus and T. Durieux, "Wolves in the repository: A software engineering analysis of the XZ Utils supply chain attack," in Proc. IEEE/ACM 22nd Int. Conf. Mining Software Repositories (MSR), 2025.
contrib: Reconstructs the XZ Utils backdoor (CVE-2024-3094): a patient maintainer takeover plus build-script payload.
gap: Authority changes and build-time payloads are the attack surface; Loom's continuity + sandbox target both.

cite: C. Miller, C. Kästner, and B. Vasilescu, "'We feel like we're winging it:' A study on navigating open-source dependency abandonment," in Proc. 31st ACM ESEC/FSE, 2023.
contrib: Interviews with 33 developers: abandonment is common and users have no game plan for it.
gap: Abandoned (orphaned) packages are the entry point for adoption attacks; Loom detects the change of authority.

cite: T. R. Schorlemmer et al., "Signing in four public software package registries: Quantity, quality, and influencing factors," in Proc. IEEE Symp. Security and Privacy (SP), 2024.
contrib: Measures signing in Maven, PyPI, DockerHub and Hugging Face: adoption is low unless mandated, quality depends on tooling.
gap: Signing proves who published, not that the artifact matches its source; Loom adds k-of-n reproducible attestations.

cite: K. Merrill, Z. Newman, S. Torres-Arias, and K. Sollins, "Speranza: Usable, privacy-friendly software signing," in Proc. ACM SIGSAC Conf. Computer and Communications Security (CCS), 2023.
contrib: Identity-based signing with signer anonymity via zero-knowledge co-commitments; <1 ms sign/verify.
gap: Requires registry cooperation; the AUR offers none, so Loom must work with zero cooperation (CON-1).

cite: E. Abu Ishgair, M. S. Melara, and S. Torres-Arias, "SoK: A defense-oriented evaluation of software supply chain security," arXiv:2405.14993, 2024.
contrib: Evaluates supply-chain defences by the attacks they actually stop; argues for layered, composable defences.
gap: Supports Loom's defence-in-depth design, evaluated by ablation (E4).

cite: M. Tamanna, S. Hamer, M. Tran, S. Fahl, Y. Acar, and L. Williams, "Analyzing challenges in deployment of the SLSA framework for software supply chain security," arXiv:2409.05014, 2024.
contrib: 1,523 SLSA issues across 233 repositories: complex implementation and unclear communication block adoption.
gap: Provenance frameworks need producer buy-in; Loom produces provenance itself via independent rebuilders.

cite: J. Malka, S. Zacchiroli, and T. Zimmermann, "Reproducibility of build environments through space and time," in Proc. 46th IEEE/ACM ICSE: New Ideas and Emerging Results, 2024.
contrib: Rebuilt 99.94% of 14k packages from a 6-year-old Nixpkgs revision; build environments can be reproduced.
gap: Shows independent rebuilding is feasible, which is the premise of Loom's Thread rebuilders.

cite: J. Malka, S. Zacchiroli, and T. Zimmermann, "Does functional package management enable reproducible builds at scale? Yes.," in Proc. IEEE/ACM 22nd Int. Conf. Mining Software Repositories (MSR), 2025.
contrib: Rebuilt 709,816 Nix packages: bitwise reproducibility is achievable at ecosystem scale.
gap: Reproducibility is measured but not turned into an install-time trust decision; Weave does that.

cite: H. Malvai et al., "Parakeet: Practical key transparency for end-to-end encrypted messaging," in Proc. Network and Distributed System Security Symp. (NDSS), 2023.
contrib: Production-grade transparency log with witness-style consistency, without consensus.
gap: Transparency without blockchain is practical; Loom applies it to build attestations (Warp).

cite: J. Len, M. Chase, E. Ghosh, K. Laine, and R. Cruz Moreno, "OPTIKS: An optimized key transparency system," in Proc. 33rd USENIX Security Symp., 2024.
contrib: Scalable transparency with smaller storage and strong consistency guarantees.
gap: Confirms Merkle-log transparency scales; Loom adds split-view detection via witness cross-checks.

cite: M. Alhindi and J. Hallett, "Sandboxing adoption in open source ecosystems," in Proc. 12th ACM/IEEE Int. Workshop on Software Engineering for Systems-of-Systems and Software Ecosystems (SESoS), 2024.
contrib: Fewer than 1% of packages directly use seccomp, Landlock, Capsicum, Pledge or Unveil.
gap: Sandboxing is rarely applied by developers; Loom applies it at the package manager for every build.

cite: S. R. Brandt et al., "Locking down science gateways with Landlock and seccomp," in Proc. 59th Hawaii Int. Conf. System Sciences (HICSS), 2026, pp. 7413–7422.
contrib: Applies Landlock + seccomp to confine real scientific codes with low overhead.
gap: Validates the unprivileged Landlock + seccomp combination that Heddle's reduced tier relies on.
